trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender
trusted_external_entities.description: Entity initiating transactions that may invoke SELFDESTRUCT opcode
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Transaction sender is authenticated via ECDSA signature verification but can submit arbitrary contract calls including SELFDESTRUCT operations. The EIP-6780 same-transaction check provides additional validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer
trusted_external_entities.description: Miner or entity producing blocks with PoW solutions
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Block producers can submit invalid PoW solutions and must be verified through full Ethash validation. The protocol assumes adversarial block producers and validates all submitted proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client
trusted_external_entities.description: Resource-constrained client verifying PoW without full DAG
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Light clients receive data from untrusted sources and must validate using cache-based verification. They operate in adversarial network conditions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Calling contract is EVM-validated bytecode that has passed deployment checks. However, it may attempt to manipulate gas or memory parameters, requiring runtime validation of memory bounds.

trusted_external_entities.name: Called Contract
trusted_external_entities.description: Sub-routine that returns data constrained to output bounds
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Called contract is EVM-validated but can return arbitrary data. The output bounds enforcement prevents memory corruption outside designated areas.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.description: External client making JSON-RPC requests to Ethereum node
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: RPC clients are external network entities that can send malformed requests, attempt injection attacks, or submit invalid data. All input must be validated before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.description: Entity submitting transactions via eth_sendTransaction or eth_sendRawTransaction
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Transaction submitters can attempt to submit invalid or malicious transactions. While raw transactions are signature-validated, the submission endpoint itself must handle malformed input safely.

security_assumptions: Transaction signature is valid ECDSA
Same-transaction check prevents legacy SELFDESTRUCT behavior post-Cancun
Balance transfer to beneficiary is atomic
Full nodes verify complete PoW before accepting blocks
Invalid PoW results in block rejection without state changes
DAG regeneration at epoch boundaries is deterministic
Cache provides equivalent security to full DAG verification
Light client correctly regenerates cache at epoch boundaries
Verification result is deterministic
Gas charging prevents unbounded memory expansion
Memory parameters are validated as valid 256-bit integers
Output bounds enforcement prevents arbitrary memory writes
Return data is bounded by output_size parameter
Memory write is limited to designated output area
Dynamic return size (2^256-1) is handled safely
JSON parsing handles malformed input safely
Method whitelist prevents unauthorized operations
Parameter validation occurs before execution
Rate limiting prevents DoS attacks
Raw transactions require valid ECDSA signature
Transaction format validation occurs before mempool insertion
Nonce validation prevents replay attacks
Gas price/limit validation prevents resource exhaustion
